contract.note: Reading 'persist' as 'still present, not unchanged' and using late 2024 as the period is an ordinary reading. Because 'persist' has no severity threshold, the interpretation drives the result.

evidence.note: October 2024 Apple GSM-Symbolic study: fragile reasoning across state-of-the-art models. Within the period.
SimpleQA, October 2024: top models answered under half correctly. The questions were chosen adversarially, which overstates the error rate, but it still shows factuality gaps.
ARC Prize, December 2024: o3 still fails some very easy tasks, so reasoning gaps remained.
Shows a large jump in o3's reasoning in December 2024, but not that the weaknesses were gone. Context only, not a contradiction.

reviews.rationale: Late-2024 evidence shows reasoning and factuality failures persisting in frontier models (e1–e3). o3's progress (e4) does not show the weaknesses were solved. No compositionality-specific evaluation was read, so that item rests indirectly on the reasoning results, but nothing contradicts it.

contract.note: Plain reading (no method reliably stops confident false outputs across ordinary tasks by the end of 2024) is fair and ordinary.

Same paper: GPT-4o and Claude score under 50% on SimpleQA. The questions are adversarial, but it is inconsistent with a robust solution.

reviews.rationale: In late 2024, OpenAI's own researchers described hallucination as an unsolved open problem, with frontier models below 50% on a factuality benchmark. The packet contains nothing showing a robust fix by the end of 2024. Independent leaderboard data was not read, but the lab's own admission of limits meets the support condition.

contract.note: Broad independent acceptance as the test for AGI, with self-declared financial definitions excluded, matches the speaker's own framing and is an ordinary reading.

evidence.note: Independent year-end review, published January 2026 (before the evaluation date): judged Musk's 'smarter than any human in 2025' mostly false.

Musk, January 2026, still treats human-surpassing AI as a future event. This implies it had not happened in 2025, but it is indirect and not an independent finding.

reviews.rationale: The horizon ended on 31 December 2025. Independent assessments found no system accepted as AGI or as smarter than any human during 2025 (e1, e2). Even Musk placed it in the future in January 2026 (e3). The packet contains no widely accepted AGI claim.

evidence.note: OpenAI's April 2025 system card (a company disclosure about its own limits): o3 and o4-mini hallucinate at substantial rates on PersonQA, higher than o1.
OpenAI paper, September 2025: hallucinations persist even in state-of-the-art systems.
Independent report, October 2025: fabricated citations led Deloitte to partly refund a government contract. A consequential incident during the horizon.
OpenAI's claimed relative cuts in factual errors for GPT-5 show progress, not elimination. The same article calls hallucination a major problem.

reviews.rationale: Through 2025, labs reported material hallucination rates and called the problem persistent (e1, e2), and there was a documented costly incident (e3). GPT-5's reductions (e4) show improvement, not that the problem stopped being material. The support condition is met.
